thread:
sam (sales): Heads-up: MerchantOnramp sent a traffic CSV + their security questionnaire. They want a 2-week POC that proves sustained peak handling and an ops handoff for a reserved pool. Need sizing, failover plan, and a cost delta for reserved vs burst.

nina (solutions): Summary of traffic: weekday 18:00-21:00 local has 120 qps sustained, occasional spikes to 480 qps for ~2-6 minutes, mean token payload ~350. Mostly multi-turn chat with attachments.

lee (eng-infra): Initial take: baseline for 120 qps @350 tokens = 1.5 A40-equivalents (round up to 2 for safety). To hit 480 qps short spikes need an extra 3 A40s. Recommend 2 reserved + burst pool of 3 (burst credits). Use warm standby rather than cold autoscale to meet <250ms p95 SLA.

tara (security): Questionnaire highlights: they require customer-managed KMS (AWS CloudHSM acceptable), syslog export to their SIEM, and proof of key rotation policy. They also want data classification notes for audit. Private control plane is preferred.

maria (cs): POC acceptance criteria they emailed: 1) p95 <300ms for sustained load, 2) graceful degrade to reduced model w/out errors, 3) no PII in external logs, 4) SSO + SCIM repro. Also they want runbook for AZ failover.

lee (eng-infra): Ops plan sketch:
- Reserved pool: 2 A40-eqs (baseline).
- Burst pool: 3 A40-eqs on warm standby (prestarted but scaled to zero GPU work queues).
- Autoscale: instant attach of burst nodes via warm routing; prefer warm start to meet short burst targets.
- Model strategy: baseline FP16, fallback INT8 quantized for bursts.
- KV warm: run short prefix warm-up 10m pre-peak using sample prompts.
- Backpressure: circuit at 1500 concurrent inflight requests, reject with 429 and retry-after header.

nina (solutions): For POC we should run mixed-mode test: simulated day with 3 real spike windows, measure p95 and token cost. Provide a replay harness with their sample CSV.

billing-bot: Quote stub generated: reserved(2 A40) + burst credits(3 A40 for peaks) => monthly delta estimate: $RES_DELTA (placeholder). PAYG burn for same spikes estimated ~1.55x higher. Formal quote pending finance.

tara (security): On KMS/HSM: we can support AWS CloudHSM and external HSM via BYOK. Willing to export audit logs to S3 with encryption. I'll draft answers and include key rotation schedule. Need architecture diagram for Private plane + VPC peering.

maria (cs): I'll collect their SSO metadata and SIEM endpoints. Also ask which data fields they consider regulated so we can exclude from logs.

sam (sales): Nice. Two questions before I reply to the customer: 1) how long to craft the ops runbook and cost numbers? 2) what are failure modes and RTOs we promise during POC?

lee (eng-infra): Runbook draft + failover matrix by tomorrow EOD. Failure modes: node eviction -> failover to quantized model within 20-40s (depends on queue), AZ loss -> route to alternate AZ with cold-warm startup ~90-120s (we'll show mitigation using cross-AZ warm standbys).

tara (security): Questionnaire draft in 48 hours. Diagram in 72 hours.

nina (solutions): I'll prepare the replay harness and test plan today, include sample prompts and success metrics.

billing-bot: Reminder: reserved SKUs require finance approval for discounts. Placeholder quote will not bind.

sam (sales): Great. I'll send a short reply to MerchantOnramp summarizing: baseline 2 reserved A40s, burst pool + warm standby, FP16 baseline with INT8 fallback, KV preheat, POC acceptance criteria, security next steps. Will attach ETA on full quote and runbook.

tara (security): Please add me to the thread with the customer when you send the security checklist.

maria (cs): Proposed check-in cadence during POC: daily standup + a mid-POC deep dive.

sam (sales): Done. I'll cc @tara and @lee. Planning to send tonight. :rocket:
